prompt_policy.role: Structured anatomical applicability prior, not an individual diagnosis or a fixed edge sign.

prompt_policy.freeze_rule: Corrected protocol is frozen after implementation audit; previous invalid results were already observed and are not a blinded preregistration.

concepts.prompt_text: At the group level, some autistic individuals exhibit convergent negative normative functional connectivity deviations involving sensorimotor and attention-associated regions. Such convergence is heterogeneous and must not be interpreted as universal hypoconnectivity of every connection attached to these regions.
concepts.source_title: Ilioska et al., Nature Mental Health (2026)
concepts.evidence_scale: population region/network convergence; not a fixed edge

concepts.td_reference_text: In neurotypical participants with comparable age, sex, scanning site and motion conditions, functional connectivity variability should be evaluated against a learned normative reference. Deviation from that reference alone is not a diagnosis of autism.

concepts.prompt_text: Regional convergence of positive normative connectivity deviations has been reported in portions of medial prefrontal, cingulate and inferior parietal areas in some autistic populations. The observation is population-level and should not be imposed as a mandatory positive deviation for every patient or individual edge.
concepts.source_title: Ilioska et al., Nature Mental Health (2026)
concepts.evidence_scale: population regional convergence; not a fixed edge
concepts.supported_direction: weak positive population prior; individual signs remain free
not_supported_claims: DMN identity without independent network mapping
concepts.td_reference_text: Observed deviations in medial prefrontal, cingulate and parietal regions should be compared with conditional neurotypical expectations while retaining uncertainty about the underlying functional system and individual deviation direction.

concepts.prompt_text: Atypical connectivity involving subcortical and cortical regions may contribute to distributed functional differences in subsets of autistic individuals. Its spatial distribution and direction are heterogeneous, and sparse observed connectivity provides incomplete evidence for the underlying neural system.
concepts.source_title: Ilioska et al. (2026); Kobbersmed et al. (2026)
concepts.td_reference_text: Subcortical-cortical connectivity should be evaluated against a neurotypical reference conditional on measured demographic and acquisition variables, without assuming that atypicality in any single observed connection identifies autism.
